name: aseprite-mcp

tools.name: status
tools.description: Shows the Aseprite executable in use, its version, and whether a live Aseprite is connected to the bridge.

tools.name: install_extension
tools.description: Copies the bridge extension into Aseprite's user extensions folder. A running Aseprite must be restarted to load it.

tools.name: launch_aseprite
tools.description: Starts the Aseprite GUI with the bridge extension and waits for it to connect, enabling live mode. The first time, Aseprite asks to allow the script's network and file access; tick 'Give full trust' / 'Don't show again' in that dialog.

waitSeconds.description: How long to wait for the bridge (default 30)

tools.name: run_lua
tools.description: Runs Lua code inside Aseprite with the full scripting API (app, Sprite, Image, Layer, Color, ...). Globals: `args` (your args object), `sprite` (resolved sprite or app.sprite), `MCP` (helper runtime: MCP.color(), MCP.layer(spr, ref), MCP.sprite_info(spr) ...). `print` output is captured. The `return` value is sent back as JSON. Use api_docs for the API reference.

code.description: Lua source. Use `return` to send a value back.

sprite.description: File path, open tab title, or sprite id. Defaults to the active sprite (live). Batch mode needs a file path.

args.description: Values available to the code as `args`

mutates.description: Batch mode: false skips saving the sprite afterwards (default true)

save.description: Batch mode: write changes back to the sprite file (default true)

backend.description: auto (default): live Aseprite if connected, else headless batch

tools.name: run_command
tools.description: Executes any Aseprite menu command (app.command.<name>) with parameters, e.g. Flip, Rotate, Outline, BrightnessContrast, ColorQuantization, LinkCels, ReverseFrames, AutocropSprite. See list_commands for names and parameters. Strings like '#ff0000' become Colors; {x,y,width,height} becomes a Rectangle. ui=false is added unless allowUi is true.

sprite.description: File path, open tab title, or sprite id. Defaults to the active sprite (live). Batch mode needs a file path.

layer.description: Layer to make active before running

frame.description: Frame to make active before running

allowUi.description: Let the command open its dialog (live mode only)

mutates.description: Batch mode: false skips saving (default true)

save.description: Batch mode: write changes back to the sprite file (default true)

backend.description: auto (default): live Aseprite if connected, else headless batch

tools.name: list_commands
tools.description: Lists Aseprite commands usable with run_command, with their parameters (extracted from the Aseprite source).

tools.name: api_docs
tools.description: Reads the Aseprite Lua API reference (bundled from github.com/aseprite/api). Without a topic, lists topics. Topics include app, sprite, layer, cel, image, color, palette, tag, slice, tileset, selection, dialog, websocket, and command/<CommandName>.

tools.name: cli
tools.description: Runs the Aseprite command line in batch mode (aseprite -b <args>) and returns its output. Useful for --sheet/--data exports, --split-layers, --list-tags, --save-as with {layer}/{frame} templates, --scale, --color-mode, etc. See https://www.aseprite.org/docs/cli/.

instructions:
Controls Aseprite (pixel art editor) through its Lua scripting API.

Two backends:
- live: a running Aseprite GUI with the bridge extension connected. Changes show up on screen, the active sprite/layer/frame/selection persist between calls, undo works. Start it with launch_aseprite.
- batch: a headless "aseprite -b" process per call. Pass 'sprite' as a file path; mutating tools save the file back (set save=false to skip). Selection, undo history and unsaved sprites do not survive between batch calls.
'auto' (default) uses live when connected, else batch.

Conventions: coordinates are canvas pixels with (0,0) at top-left. Frames, layer indices and tag/slice indices are 1-based; palette indices are 0-based.
Colors: "#rrggbb", "#rrggbbaa", names (red, transparent...), a palette index number, or {r,g,b,a}.
Layers: name, "Group/Child" path, or the index from get_sprite_info.

Workflow tips: get_sprite_info to learn the structure; render_preview to look at the result; get_pixels returns a compact character grid + legend, and draw_pixels accepts the same rows+legend format for pixel art. use_tool runs any Aseprite tool (pencil, line, rectangle, ellipse, paint_bucket, spray, gradient, contour, polygon, curve, blur, jumble, marquee tools...).
Anything not covered by a dedicated tool: run_command executes any of the ~180 menu commands (list_commands shows names and params), and run_lua runs arbitrary Lua with the full API (api_docs has the reference).
